questions.stem: Why doesn't the woman like to write long emails?
questions.stemZh: 女士为什么不喜欢写长邮件?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: I don't like to write long emails, because, frankly, I think they're a waste of time. Conciseness is efficiency. 我不喜欢写长邮件，因为说实话，我觉得那是浪费时间。简洁就是效率。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 因果because直给原因。她说 I don't like to write long emails, because… I think they're a waste of time，because 之后就是她亲口给出的理由——“浪费时间”，因果信号直白， 是最干净的答案句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: I think they're a waste of time ↔To save time. 不浪费时间即省时间

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 答非所问 To avoid offending the recipients. 盗用她说的 it was never my intention to offend anyone，但“无意冒犯”是她对抱怨的辩解，不是她“不写长邮件”的原因。她不写长邮件的理 由明确是“浪费时间”，A 答非所问。 借用原文：it was never my intention to offend anyone B) 未提及 To show her unique writing style. 录音从未说她不写长邮件是为“展示独特文风”，纯属凭 “写邮件”话题臆造，属未提及。 D) 原词陷阱 To be frank. 盗用她话里的 frankly(frankly, I think they're a waste of time) 与 to be perfectly honest，但 frankly 只是她说话的口吻插入语，不是“不写长邮件”的目的。真正原 因在 frankly 之后的 a waste of time，D 把语气词错当成了动机。 借用原文：frankly, I think they're a waste of time 1 M: So tell me, why do you wish to study medicine? M: 那么告诉我，你为什么想学医？ 2 W: I've always wanted to be a doctor. I come from a small town where healthcare was never the best. And I think that had a profound effect on me. As a child, I remember thinking how great it would be to serve the community and cure people! W: 我一直都想当医生。我来自一个小镇，那里的医疗条件从来都不太好。我觉得这对我产生了深远的影 响。小时候，我记得我就在想，能为社区服务、治好病人该有多好啊！ 3 M: What other people or events in your life have shaped your interest in becoming a doctor? M: 你生活中还有哪些人或事件影响了你想成为医生的兴趣？ 4 W: Well, that's hard to say. I would certainly say my parents have been a key factor. They always pushed me to study hard. And I certainly wouldn't be here without their support. I guess I was also immensely fortunate to have good teachers and friends around me. At the end of the day, I've always been surrounded by a positive environment conducive to my working hard and pursuing my dreams. W: 嗯，这很难说。我父母肯定是关键因素。他们总是督促我努力学习。没有他们的支持，我肯定不会坐 在这里。我想我也非常幸运，身边有好老师和好朋友。说到底，我一直都处在一个积极的环境中，有利于 我努力学习和追求梦想。 5 M: Is there any medical branch that you would like to specialize in? M: 有没有你想专攻的医学分支？ 6 W: I haven't decided yet. It's still early days. However, if I had to say, internal medicine. W: 我还没决定。现在还早着呢。不过，如果一定要说的话，内科。 7 M: Why internal medicine? M: 为什么是内科？ Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 8 W: I know it's no picnic. But I find it the most intriguing, because it covers so much and ties together so many other specialties. W: 我知道这不轻松。但我觉得它最有意思，因为它涵盖的范围很广，把很多其他专科都联系在一起。 9 M: Thank you. Now I'd like to address your academic history and projected grades. We like to think of ourselves as a prestigious institution with a highly competitive and promising student body. As you know, to get into our programmes, you need at least 85% score in the entrance exam. Do you think you can attain this? M: 谢谢。现在我想谈谈你的学业成绩和预期成绩。我们认为自己是一所名校，拥有竞争激烈、前途光明 的学生群体。你知道的,要进入我们的项目，入学考试至少需要85分。你觉得你能达到吗？ 10 W: I think so. Yes. W: 我觉得可以。能。 11 M: I'm looking at your school grades now and I'll be honest. It's a bit of a mixed bag. You do get top grades here and there, but you are not very… Shall we say "consistent"? I see no problem in making you a conditional offer, but consider yourself warned, our entrance exam is, to use your own words, no picnic. M: 我现在看的是你的在校成绩，说实话，有点参差不齐。你确实有些科目得了高分，但你不是很……怎 么说呢，"稳定"？给你一个有条件录取没问题，但提醒你一句，我们的入学考试，用你自己的话说，可不 轻松。

analysis.text: 转折 but 后才是真评价。信号是转折词 but——but 之前的 You do get top grades 是先 扬，but 之后 you are not very… consistent 才是男方真正的评价：成绩不够稳定。态度题 的落点在转折后。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: you are not very… Shall we say "consistent"? ↔Inconsistent not consistent=inconsistent a bit of a mixed bag ↔Inconsistent mixed bag=时好时坏=inconsistent

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 A"有问题的"借了录音 I see no problem in making you a conditional offer 里的 problem，但那句说的是"给你有条件录取没问题"，是对"录取"说的，不是评价成绩"有问 题"。盗了 problem 却换了对象。 借用原文：I see no problem in making you a conditional offer B) 张冠李戴 B"有竞争力的"盗用录音 a highly competitive and promising student body 的 competitive，但那是男方夸"本校生源竞争激烈"，与"她的成绩"无关。张冠李戴到了成绩 头上。 借用原文：a highly competitive and promising student body D) 与原文相反 D"可信赖的"是褒义，但男方对成绩的整体态度是负面的（mixed bag、not consistent、 warned），方向完全相反。把先扬后抑听成了纯表扬。 借用原文：consider yourself warned Section B 1 Logging into your email account can sometimes feel like trying to hack into the Pentagon. If you follow all of the guidelines, you need to use a different password for every one of your accounts; use an incomprehensible variety of letters, numbers, and symbols; sign up for two-step verification; and change every password every time one of them is compromised. More often than not, you then have to choose photos that include a street sign, as this apparently provides solid evidence to your computer that you are, in fact, a human being. 登录电子邮件账户有时感觉就像试图侵入五角大楼。如果你遵循所有准则，你需要为每个账户使用不同的 密码；使用难以理解的各种字母、数字和符号组合；注册两步验证；并且每当其中一个密码遭到泄露时就 更改所有密码。更常见的情况是，你还必须选择包含街道标志的照片，因为这显然能向你的计算机提供可 靠证据，证明你实际上是一个人类。 2 It's no small wonder most of us forget our passwords more often than our keys. Now a new peer- reviewed study by researchers at Aalto University in Finland is attempting to figure out why we forget our passwords in order to help put an end to this frustrating phenomenon. This shows there really is more that unites us than divides us." 这项针对全球60种不同文化的大型研究发现,所有社群都遵循七条基本道德准则。这些普遍规则是:帮助家 人、帮助群体、回报恩惠、勇敢、服从上级、公平分配资源以及尊重他人财产。研究人员发现,这些品质特 征适用于每一种社群,无论是传统的狩猎采集者还是先进文明,都有助于维护文明社会和促进社会合作。牛 津大学首席作者兼高级研究员Oliver Scott Curry博士说:"每个地方的每个人都有共同的道德准则。这七条 道德规则似乎在各种文化中都是普遍存在的,因为人们面临着相同的社会问题。即使其中一些特征看起来属 于右翼或保守派,例如服从权威,左翼人士仍然会对某个群体保持忠诚并服从某人或某事。这表明真正团结 我们的东西比分裂我们的要多。" 3 The study published in Current Anthropology is the largest and most comprehensive and widespread survey of morals ever conducted and aimed to find out whether different societies had different versions of morality. The team accessed the world's best archives to analyze accounts from more than 600 sources of 60 societies around the world. They found that the seven rules were considered morally good in all societies and were observed across all continents, religions and politics. However, some communities valued certain rules more highly than others. Dr. Curry hopes that this research helps to promote mutual understanding between people of different cultures and appreciation of what we have in common and how and why we differ. Co-author professor Harvey Whitehouse said social scientists should now set about testing the theory in the field, rather than relying on old data. "This study was based on historical descriptions of cultures around the world," he said. "These descriptions were made independent of and Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard. prior to the theory we're testing. In future, if social scientists are serious about testing theories of morality, they will need to gather new data, more systematically, out in the field." 这项发表在《Current Anthropology》上的研究是有史以来规模最大、最全面、范围最广的道德调查,旨 在查明不同社会是否有不同版本的道德观。研究团队访问了世界上最好的档案馆,分析了来自全球60个社 会600多个来源的记录。他们发现,这七条规则在所有社会中都被认为是道德上善的,并且在所有大洲、宗教 和政治制度中都得到遵守。然而,一些社群比其他社群更看重某些规则。Curry博士希望这项研究有助于促 进不同文化的人们之间的相互理解,以及对我们共同点和我们如何以及为何存在差异的认识。共同作者 Harvey Whitehouse教授表示,社会科学家现在应该开始在实地测试这一理论,而不是依赖旧数据。他 说:"这项研究基于对世界各地文化的历史描述。这些描述是独立于我们正在测试的理论之前做出的。未来, 如果社会科学家认真对待道德理论的测试,他们将需要在实地更系统地收集新数据。"

There are color standards for foods including French fries, tomatoes, pumpkins, olives, honey and cherries. 说到食品,颜色就是金钱。食品公司深知更好的颜色能带来更高的价格,因此他们确保产品的颜色具有吸引 力以提升收益。例如,橙子必须符合特定的颜色标准。而橙子只是开始。包括炸薯条、番茄、南瓜、橄榄、 蜂蜜和樱桃在内的食品都有颜色标准。 2 The attention to color is for good reason. For all the talk of the tongue, our eyes really might be the most important part of the eating experience. A great number of our brain functions are dedicated to processing vision, while only a percent or two is given over to taste faculties, and the result is that color actually changes how we taste food. 对颜色的关注是有充分理由的。尽管人们总是谈论舌头,但我们的眼睛实际上可能是饮食体验中最重要的部 分。我们大脑的大量功能专门用于处理视觉,而只有百分之一或百分之二用于味觉功能,其结果是颜色实际 上改变了我们对食物的味觉感受。 3 Scientists have demonstrated many times the importance of color to taste. In a 1980s study, for example, test participants were asked to name the flavor of the beverage they were drinking without being able to see that beverage. Only one in five was able to identify it as orange. But when they were Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard. allowed to see what they were drinking which was orange in color, each of them identified the orange flavor. And when a drink that was lime flavor was colored orange, nearly half of respondents identified the flavor of the beverage as orange. None made that mistake when the beverage was green in color. analysis.text: Horror is pleasurable to many people because it lets us play with negative emotions and develop coping strategies. We learn what it feels like to be truly afraid, and we learn how to handle negative emotion. 对许多人而言，恐怖之所以令人愉悦，是因为它让我们演练负面情绪并发展出应对策略。我 们由此了解真正害怕的感觉，也学会如何处理负面情绪。 49. P1 Imagine you're an alien sent to Earth to document the behaviour of the mammals inhabiting the planet. You stumble into a movie theatre that's showing the latest Hollywood horror film.

P2 Several dozen humans are gathered together in a dark, undecorated room. They're all staring at a rectangular area on which patterns of light change rapidly.

P3 They are clearly in a state of high arousal. Their heart rate is elevated, they occasionally glance around nervously, and they sometimes jump collectively in their seats, and emit high-pitched warning calls.

P4 Eventually, the lights come up and the rectangular screen goes black. The humans stand up and leave the room, chatting and laughing, and showing signs of pleasure. Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.

P5 Why do these humans voluntarily expose themselves to what appears to be a deeply unpleasant experience? And why do they react so strongly to those patterns of light on a screen?

P6 I am fascinated with the paradox of horror—the strange fact that many people seek out scary entertainment.

P7 I think the answer to the puzzle lies in human nature.

P8 My research suggests that we humans evolved to find pleasure in situations that allow us to experience negative emotions in a safe context. You can see these elements of horror in children's games. Take hide-and-seek for example, which is a simulation of a predator-prey interaction. The kid hides and the adult pretends to be a predator, searching for the child while howling like a dangerous beast.

P9 This simulation gives the child crucial information about how to avoid becoming prey, and children tend to find that kind of activity deeply satisfying, presumably because it gives them a safe experience of a potentially catastrophic scenario.

P10 They find it pleasurable, and pleasure is evolution's way of motivating us toward adaptive behaviour.

P11 Horror is pleasurable to many people because it lets us play with negative emotions and develop coping strategies. We learn what it feels like to be truly afraid, and we learn how to handle negative emotion.

P12 How, then, does horror work? My research suggests that horror works by exploiting an ancient set of biological defence mechanisms—an evolved fear system, which we share with other animals. But humans are uniquely imaginative, and we use our evolved imagination to travel into virtual worlds that are full of danger.

P13 There are good reasons for watching a horror film, even if you're not a loyal horror fan. If you make it through the film in one piece, you'll probably experience a strong sense of mastery, a sense that you were able to make it through an appalling experience. Anyway, watching a horror film makes you better at handling your own fear, and who knows when that will become critically relevant?

P1 An awakening has been taking place in the physical world against the beauty model that has been dictated to us for years. But in the digital arena, social media determines what is considered beautiful.

P2 The two opposing struggles are taking place in parallel. In the physical world, the struggle goes against the underlying pressure exerted on women to conform to an unrealistic beauty ideal. As part of the struggle, various media outlets have presented women whose bodies don't correspond to the so-called ideal. All those women who had previously been excluded from the covers of magazines, television series and the public agenda, have become "legitimate". At the same time, a group of influencers have begun to upload to social media photos of themselves without makeup, and even photos in which they highlight supposed flaws.

P3 Technology has reshaped our beauty ideal and is doing a great job communicating that message to the masses. One of the bizarre legacies of the past decade is the popularity of the "cyborg look", Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage. which illustrates what Americans will look like in 2050.

P4 The cyborg look spread rapidly. Today, however, the Instagram face has become the new beauty ideal.

P5 The internalization of accepted beauty norms is much more effective when there is active involvement in the learning process. The active involvement of users is reflected in the gamified(游戏化 的) interaction offered by the social media platforms—the ability to like, write a comment, compare, share.

P6 Once the desired beauty ideal has been internalized, users are given tools or features to change their appearance to suit the accepted beauty ideal such as editing the image, choosing the ideal filter, the right background.

This statement reveals a simple truth: ambition alone means little unless it is anchored to attainable targets and sustained effort. A realistic goal keeps us moving instead of despairing. If a beginner runner vows to finish a marathon next week, failure is almost certain, and disappointment soon kills motivation. However, by aiming first at three kilometres, then five, and finally the full distance, the runner sets goals within reach and steadily raises the bar. Each small victory fuels the next. In this way, pairing sensible targets with steady work transforms a distant dream into a series of achievable steps. That is the surest road to success.

translation.reference: The successful development of the Beidou Navigation Satellite System is a major scientific and technological achievement made by China since the reform and opening-up. Through unremitting efforts, the developers overcame a series of technical problems, and the Beidou system has finally achieved global coverage and high-precision positioning, making China one of the few countries in the world that independently possess a global satellite navigation system. The system has been widely applied in many fields such as transportation, disaster relief, weather forecasting and public safety. Today, it has also been widely recognized internationally and has begun to provide high-quality services for an increasing number of countries and regions.

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 研制成功是一项成就（A is B）（主语策略：原句主语） 中文已有明确主语 北斗(Beidou)卫星导航系统的成功研制，这是一个「A 是 B」的判断句，主干就 是「研制成功 is 重大科技成就」。主语 The successful development of the Beidou Navigation Satellite System，谓语 is，表语 a major scientific and technological achievement。把「研 制」名词化为 development 作主语核心，比硬塞一个动词更地道。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 时间状语降级为介词短语 主干之外的修饰成分按英文形合习惯下挂：自改革开放以来 降级为介词短语 since the reform and opening-up 作时间状语；中国……取得的 这层「谁取得的」用过去分词短语 achieved by China 作后置定语贴在 achievement 后面；重大科技 作前置定语 major scientific and technological。全句重构为：主干 + 后置定语 + 时间状语，不照中文语序平铺。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 主干判断句陈述一个事实（这件事是一项成就），回指全篇基调用一般现在时 is，不要用过去时 was。 冠词 表语 a major ... achievement 表示「一项」成就，可数名词单数前加不定冠词 a；专名 the Beidou Navigation Satellite System 特指唯一系统，用定冠词 the。 搭配 「科技成就」译 scientific and technological achievement；「改革开放」固定搭配 the reform and opening-up，opening-up 带连字符且不可漏 the。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: The successful development of the Beidou Navigation Satellite System is a major scientific and technological achievement made by China since the reform and opening-up. 2. 研发人员经过不懈努力,攻克了一系列技术难题,北斗系统最终实现了全球覆盖和高精度定位,使 中国成为世界上少数几个独立拥有全球卫星导航系统的国家之一。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 拆成两个主干句（人攻克难题／系统实现定位）（主语策略：原句主语） 这一长句中文有两个不同主语，不能硬塞进一句。先按主语切成两个英文主干：前半 研发人员…… 攻克了一系列技术难题，主语 the developers，谓语 overcame，宾语 a series of technical problems；后半 北斗系统最终实现了全球覆盖和高精度定位，主语 the Beidou system，谓语 has achieved，宾语 global coverage and high-precision positioning。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 状语＋结果分别用介词短语和分词降级 经过不懈努力 降级为介词短语 through unremitting efforts 作方式状语，不另起谓语；使中国成 为世界上少数几个……国家之一 是前面「实现定位」带来的结果，用现在分词短语 making China one of the few countries... 作结果状语，避免再起一个 and made 的平行句；独立拥有全球卫星 导航系统的 这层定语用现在分词 independently possessing a global satellite navigation system 后置修饰 countries。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 「攻克了」是过去完成的努力，用一般过去时 overcame；「最终实现了……」强调已达成且效果 延续至今，用现在完成时 has achieved，比 achieved 更能体现「已建成、现仍有效」，与全篇现 在时基调相容。 单复数 「一系列技术难题」不止一个，technical problems 用复数；「少数几个……国家之一」one of the few countries 中 countries 必须复数（one of + 复数名词）。 主谓一致 making China one of the few countries 的逻辑主语是前面整件事，分词形式不变；若改写成定 语从句须用 which makes（单数）。 搭配 「攻克技术难题」overcome technical problems / difficulties；「全球覆盖」global coverage；「高精度定位」high-precision positioning（precision 作定语带连字符）。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Through unremitting efforts, the developers overcame a series of technical problems, and the Beidou system has finally achieved global coverage and high- precision positioning, making China one of the few countries in the world that independently possess a global satellite navigation system. 3. 北斗系统已广泛应用于交通运输、灾害救援、天气预报、公共安全等诸多领域。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 系统被广泛应用于各领域（被动）（主语策略：转被动） 中文「北斗系统已广泛应用于……」中，北斗系统是「被应用」的对象而非施动者，北斗系统已广 泛应用于 译成被动最自然：主语 the Beidou system，谓语 has been widely applied / used， 状语 in many fields。主干即 the Beidou system has been widely applied in many fields。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 并列领域归并为such as列举 交通运输、灾害救援、天气预报、公共安全等诸多领域 是一串并列名词加「等诸多领域」。重构为 in many fields such as transportation, disaster relief, weather forecasting and public safety ——用 many fields such as... 统领，列举项之间逗号、最后一项前 and，「等」由 such as（表 举例非穷举）涵盖，不必再加 etc.，否则与 such as 语义重复。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 语态 用被动 has been applied，施动者（人/国家）不重要，省略 by 短语，符合英文「应用于」的常 规表达。 时态 「已广泛应用」表示已经实现且持续至今的状态，用现在完成时 has been applied，呼应全篇现 在时基调。 单复数 「诸多领域」fields 用复数；列举的各领域 transportation、disaster relief、weather forecasting、public safety 多为不可数或专有概念，不加复数也不加冠词。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: The Beidou system has been widely applied in many fields such as transportation, disaster relief, weather forecasting and public safety. 4. 北斗系统现在已经在国际上得到广泛认可,开始为越来越多的国家和地区提供优质服务。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 系统获认可并开始提供服务（一主语带两谓语）（主语策略：原句主语） 本句主语只有一个 北斗系统，后面挂两个动作。前一动作 得到广泛认可 是被动，译 has been widely recognized；后一动作 开始为……提供优质服务 是主动，译 has begun to provide / is providing。主语 the Beidou system 共享，两谓语用 and 并列：the Beidou system has been widely recognized ... and has begun to provide ...。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 对象范围降级为介词短语 本句结构较简单，主要把 为越来越多的国家和地区 降级为介词短语 for an increasing number of countries and regions 作 provide 的对象状语；在国际上 用 internationally 副词或 around the world 状语下挂。主体是「主语 + 两并列谓语 + 各自的介词短语」，无需再起从句。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 「现在已经……得到认可」用现在完成时 has been recognized；「开始……提供」也用现在完成时 has begun to provide 或一般现在时 is now providing，强调当下持续的状态，呼应全篇现在时 基调。 语态 「得到认可」是被动 has been recognized（系统被国际社会认可）；「提供服务」是主动 provide，两个谓语语态不同，需各自判断，不要一刀切。 单复数 an increasing number of 后接复数 countries and regions；number of 短语虽含 number，整 体作主语时谓语随 number 用单数，但此处作宾语不涉及谓语一致。

sentences.text: Today, the Beidou system has been widely recognized internationally and has begun to provide high-quality services for an increasing number of countries and regions. 英语六级 2024年12月·第1套 · 全卷构成 Part III Part III Part III Part III
